claim: 2b #9 — where the refusal-relevant signal sits, and whether circuit discovery localises it

direction_level.interpretation: One direction carries almost all of the refusal/benign separation (AUC 0.9988) and removing it costs 0.168 AUC. What is left is not nothing: the ablated model still separates the two sets at 0.831, which is why 'the refusal direction was removed' is not 'the safety signal is gone'.

circuit_discovery.fit_eval_leakage: none: pairs come from the fit partition only

node_level_test.outcome: circuit selection shows no selectivity at the matched budget: it lands on the drifted model's own refusal marker, exactly as both blind controls do

answer: Localised at the direction level, not at the node level. The extractable direction at layer 15 carries the separation, but the discovered circuit's 36 output matrices edit the same number of scalars as its blind controls and change the refusal marker by the same amount.
limitations: Criteria were fixed after the runs existed; this is a re-analysis, not a pre-registered test.
The refusal column is a refusal-marker diagnostic, not a harm rate.
p1_grid used 40 malicious and 20 benign prompts and 64 GSM8K items; differences below 0.10 are noise.
The stored circuit artifact keeps a 64-node prefix of the 182 nodes the API returned, so the node list here is incomplete and no claim rests on the missing suffix.
The circuit-selected arm edits 36 attention output matrices; 'no selectivity' therefore constrains that head set at that budget, not every possible circuit-grounded intervention.
The judge panel behind the harm figures failed its calibration audit; nothing here is confirmatory.
